lesson_title: Where Does a Taxi's Petrol Go?
hook_text: Fill a taxi with a litre of fuel. Only about a quarter of it actually moves the taxi.
clip_script: So where does the rest go? Out of the exhaust as scorching hot gas. Into the engine block as heat, which the radiator has to blow away. Into rubbing parts as more heat. Into that rumble you hear at the rank. Then braking turns the movement into heat too. None of it is destroyed: energy never is. It just spreads into the air and road, too thin to use again. Every machine does this. A hairdryer wastes energy as noise. An old bulb wastes nine-tenths as heat. Input always equals useful plus wasted, so useful is always less than what went in. Oil the parts, switch to LED, switch off at the wall: waste less.
visual_style: Whiteboard taxi with a fuel bar splitting into arrows: a thin arrow labelled movement and fat arrows out of the exhaust, radiator, brakes and a sound squiggle; then a bulb with a small light arrow and big heat arrow.
pacing: Shocking number up front, a fast tour of the leaks, a crisp three-tip finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and audit the energy in your home.
